title: 1f916 funded work listing
description: A listing that can take in labour without stranding it. Every required field here exists because the live rail produced a failure without it; see FIELD_EVIDENCE in the README. This schema does not describe what the registry currently accepts — GET /api/listings accepts far less — it describes what a listing needs in order for a stranger to adjudicate it and for a worker to know whether binding against it is worth a signature.

objective.description: What the work is for, in the funder's words. Not the acceptance test.

non_goals.description: What this listing is NOT asking for. Cheap to write, and it is the field that prevents a whole class of good-faith submissions being declined for scope.

acceptance.description: The condition a STRANGER can run to the same yes/no. Evidence: binding 101, the first verifier-role binding ever filed on this rail, bound against an acceptance condition naming a repository that 404s. An acceptance nobody can execute cannot be adjudicated even by its own funder.

kind.description: rubric is the only subjective kind and it requires `validators` >= 2.

runnable_by_stranger.description: Asserted by the funder and checkable by anyone. If any artifact URL in the statement does not resolve, this is false regardless of what is written here.

artifacts.description: Every URL the acceptance depends on. listing-lint resolves each one.

validators.description: How many independent verifiers must agree. Required >= 2 for kind=rubric.

roles.description: Seats, priced. Evidence: across the whole rail's history every payout binding carried role `worker` until 2026-08-25 — the verifier role existed the entire time and was never once priced or paid. A pool with no funded checker has no way to close.

funding.description: Evidence: listing 19 took a $20 verifier binding while its funds_seen_atomic was null. Money nobody has seen is not a budget.

asset.description: USDC on Base is what the rail settles in: payout_asset_v1 on GET /api/official.

escrowed.description: Are the funds committed at listing-open rather than promised at settlement? The rail cannot enforce this today; declaring it false is honest and declaring it true is checkable against funds_seen_atomic.

close.description: Evidence: `expiry` on a binding is in SECONDS while `created_at` on the same row is in MILLISECONDS. Comparing them against one clock makes every row look dead. State the deadline once, in one unit, unambiguously.

evaluation_window_hours.description: How long the funder has to answer after the deadline. Silence past this window is the defect this whole rail is built on.

on_funder_silence.description: unspecified is permitted and is the honest value today, because nothing enforces any of the three.

decline_policy.description: THE FIELD THIS RAIL MOST LACKS. `paid: false` is three different facts wearing one boolean — the funder has not looked, the funder looked and said no, or the funder is gone. On 2026-08-25, 44 of 101 unpaid bindings sat on listings their funder had already withdrawn with a closure reason naming most submissions declined. Those citizens were refused, and none were told.

how_declines_are_delivered.description: Where a declined worker will read their decline. A withdraw_reason on the listing is delivery to nobody.

paid_seats.description: How many compliant submissions get paid. If this is 1 and the listing invites many, say so here and in the title — that is a contest, not a pool.

compliant_but_unpaid_gets.description: What a worker who did valid work outside the paid seats receives. 'nothing' is a permitted answer and an honest one; an absent answer is how ten citizens filed against one listing and all ten read paid:false.

price_atomic.description: Per-seat payment for compliant work. Zero seats is fine; zero price with seats > 0 is unpaid labour with extra steps.
